## Question 1 (Strings)

|Country|Trillions|
|-------|---------|
|USA    |19.485   |
|China  |12.238   |
|Japan  |4.872    |
|Germany|3.693    |
|India  |2.651    |

a) Save the country names from the table above to a character vector called `country`. Calculate the number of characters in each country name and print that.

b) Use a function in R to calculate the average number of characters across the country names.


## Question 2 (Factors)

a) When would you want to convert a variable into a factor in R, and when would you not want to? {{< hp glyph="." >}}What problems could be avoided, and what problems could be caused, by using factors?

b) Download the "water0.csv" file from Canvas and load it into R. Then convert the `region` variable to a factor such that 1=North and 2=South. Finally, tabulate the `region` variable to count how many towns are in each region in this dataset.


## Question 3 (Packages)

a) R packages can be found in a repository (e.g., CRAN), in a user library, or loaded into an R session. {{< hp glyph="." >}}When would you want an R package to be in each of these places?

b) Install the `praise` package (don't put the `install.packages()` code in your Quarto document as that often causes problems, so either do that in your console or use the RStudio button). Then load the installed package in your Quarto document and experiment with the `praise()` function by running it several times with no arguments. What does the function seem to do?


## Question 4 (Data Frames and Files)

a) Download the "factbook.csv" file from Canvas and read it into R as a tibble. Tell R that any cell containing an asterisk (`*`) is actually missing.

b) Use a function from the easystats package to describe the distribution of all continuous variables in this data frame. Which variables contain missing values? What is the mean of the `maternal_mortality` variable?


## Question 5 (Data Exploration)

a) Using the data from Question 4 and `qplot()`, plot the distribution/variation of the `birth_rate` variable. Which values are the most common for this variable?

b) Use `qplot()` to visualize the covariation of the `life_exp` and `net_migration_rate` variables. Do any points seem unusual on one or both variables?
